the decrease in growth factor responsiveness observed in phenobarbitone treated mice is unlikely to be due to a decrease in epidermal growth-factor receptor expression or autophosphorylatory capacity.

phenobarbital treatment of mice causes decreased EGF responsiveness of primary hepatocytes, which is unlikely to be attributable to a decrease in receptor expression or autophosphorytion in response to growth factors.

the decrease in the growth responsiveness of hepatocytes following phenobarbitone treatment is due to an alteration in signal transduction downstream from the EGF receptor.
